title: India Post 720 for 9 at Wellington, Highest Test Total in New Zealand
excerpt: Rahul's 136 and Pant's 128 headline an innings in which each of India's top five passed 80, leaving New Zealand 33 for 1 and fighting to avoid an innings defeat.
body:
• India declared at 720 for 9 at the Basin Reserve, the highest innings total in a Test match played in New Zealand, passing New Zealand's 715 for 6 against Bangladesh at Hamilton in 2019.
  • KL Rahul made 136 and Rishabh Pant 128, and each of India's top five scored 80 or more — the first time that has happened in a Test innings.
  • New Zealand, bowled out for 368, were 33 for 1 in their second innings at tea on day four, still needing another 319 runs to avoid an innings defeat.
  • For diaspora fans: the final day starts Monday morning in Wellington, which is Sunday afternoon and evening across the United States.

India produced the biggest innings ever played on New Zealand soil on Sunday, declaring at 720 for 9 midway through the fourth afternoon of the first Test at Wellington's Basin Reserve. The total passed the previous record for a Test in New Zealand — the hosts' own 715 for 6 declared against Bangladesh at Hamilton in 2019 — and comfortably cleared the Basin Reserve ground record of 660 for 5, set by the West Indies in 1995. It is the 18th-highest innings in Test history and the third-largest in India's, behind only 759 for 7 against England at Chennai in 2016 and 726 for 9 against Sri Lanka at the Brabourne Stadium in 2009, according to SuperSport's match report.

Built by the whole top order

This was not one giant innings carrying a side; it was depth, layer on layer. Yashasvi Jaiswal (85) and KL Rahul put on 130 for the first wicket, Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal (80) added 165 for the second, and Rahul and captain Shubman Gill added 91 for the third before Rahul fell for 136 — his 13th Test hundred and his first in New Zealand. Gill was bowled by Jacob Duffy in the final over of day three for 98, two runs short of a century.

Rishabh Pant then owned the fourth morning. He put on 75 with nightwatchman Anshul Kamboj, reached his ninth Test hundred with a six, and was out off the last ball before lunch for 128 from 153 balls, with 10 fours and six sixes, as India reached the break at 629 for 6. Dhruv Jurel kept the tempo after him, scoring 78 from 79 balls before he was stumped by Tom Blundell. CricTracker noted that India also became the first team to register partnerships of 50 or more for seven or more wickets in a single innings on more than one occasion, having first done it against Australia at Ahmedabad in 2023.

New Zealand's long road back

New Zealand's first innings of 368 had been rescued from early trouble, but it left them 352 runs behind once India declared. Their second innings began the way their first had: Jasprit Bumrah bowled captain Tom Latham with the second ball of the innings, Latham's second duck of the match. Bumrah had taken 4 for 92 in the first innings, passing Javagal Srinath's 236 wickets to enter India's top ten Test wicket-takers. At tea, New Zealand were 33 for 1, needing 319 more runs simply to make India bat again, with four sessions left in the match.

What it means and what's next

India arrived in New Zealand carrying the memory of a 0-3 home defeat to the Black Caps in 2024. One innings does not settle that account, but a record 720 in Wellington, on a ground where New Zealand have historically been hard to beat, is a statement about the batting order's depth: eight partnerships of substance, runs from the openers to the lower middle order, and a wicketkeeper scoring at a strike rate most top orders would envy. The match concludes on Monday, with India needing nine wickets to convert the record innings into a 1-0 series lead.
